title: The stellarator contract: C1 and C4 hold only in vacuum; C2 and C5 on a stellarator candidate are essentially open.
text: the stellarator contract: c1 and c4 hold only in vacuum; c2 and c5 on a stellarator candidate are essentially open. plasmalean is building a lean library for stellarator design, now organized by the stellarator contract: c1 current-free rotational transform, c2 omnigeneity for thermal ions and electrons, c3 finite-β mhd stability, c4 existence, c5 thermal performance, all on one candidate. an exact non-axisymmetric vacuum field has a kam-certified torus (ι ≈ 0.137) confining field lines and passing 3.5 mev alpha guiding centres for all time (c1 and c4 in vacuum; alphas are one species, so part of c2 at most). stability (c3) is certified only on test beds that fail c1: landreman family 2 carries positive net toroidal current, and the solov'ev field is a tokamak model. c5 is shown only on that tokamak model: one field with a pressure-budget band, for every supplied transport solution. strict audit done (30 october); orbits proved to exist; weak quasisymmetry defined and the landreman families proved not weakly quasisymmetric on regions containing their axis; landreman family 1 satisfies the hypotheses of a grad counterexample (ι ≡ 2, non-generic; infrastructure); 1-d relative-entropy identity and a torus hodge period inequality; large checks rewritten as explicit proof-term certificates; heavy cells computed on a workstation and spot-checked on the laptop.

title: The aim: one candidate satisfying C1–C5 with common witnesses — not merely a non-axisymmetric field.
text: the aim: one candidate satisfying c1–c5 with common witnesses — not merely a non-axisymmetric field. tokamaks confine plasma with a large toroidal plasma current, which brings current-driven instabilities, disruptions and the need for current drive. an axisymmetric current-free field has ι = 0, so it confines nothing; a stellarator gets its rotational transform from 3-d shaping. non-axisymmetry therefore follows from c1; it is not the target. every result card in this deck is labelled with the clause it serves. plan restructured around the contract on 30 october (user-approved): goals restated, new questions q-18–q-22 on net current, drift and ε_eff, current-free finite β, definitions and thermal neoclassical bounds.

title: Small assumptions. Reusable proofs. One candidate.
text: small assumptions. reusable proofs. one candidate. physical model laws are explicit hypotheses. derived mathematics and candidate certificates live above that small domain kernel. the public library separates all six layers. the last audit found only lean/mathlib's standard logical axioms, with no added domain axioms.

title: The foundations have executable proof content.
text: the foundations have executable proof content. simple models make the definitions testable before tackling three-dimensional plasma physics. these are compiled elementary results and sanity checks, not just declarations of future tasks.

title: From a numerical proposal to a proved bound.
text: from a numerical proposal to a proved bound. rational interval soundness and contraction arguments give small end-to-end tests of the verification path. exact arithmetic is connected to mathematical soundness theorems and explicit test fixtures.

title: Two circular coils. Precisely stated regions.
text: two circular coils. precisely stated regions. the first device-specific object is a calibration fixture with symbolic positive reference current i and permeability μ₀. its field model uses ideal filaments. closure, regularity, one-turn simplicity, source separation and the nominal midpoint field have proofs.

title: Margins for the same perturbed coils and currents.
text: margins for the same perturbed coils and currents. assume closed c¹ coils with position error ≤ 1 mm, independent tangent error ≤ 1 mm/radian, and independent current errors ≤ 1% of i. manufacturing and current errors compose into continuous field and clearance certificates, not just sampled checks.

title: Maxwell identities proved; interchange stability decided both ways.
text: maxwell identities proved; interchange stability decided both ways. the closed-filament biot–savart field is divergence- and curl-free off the coil. a sharp hardy inequality gives the suydam criterion with both sufficiency and an explicit unstable mode. a realistic screw pinch (a = 1 m, r₀ = 4 m, 5 t, ⟨β⟩ = 2/75) satisfies suydam everywhere with a 25% margin, and newcomb-reduced δw ≥ 0 is certified for every mode with 1 ≤ |m| ≤ 6 (wall at the edge); phase 2 extended this to every integer (m, n) with m ≠ 0 (screwpinchmodeshighm).

title: Two exact equilibria satisfy the kernel law J × B = ∇p.
text: two exact equilibria satisfy the kernel law j × b = ∇p. the current is computed as curl b/μ₀ from actual derivatives and checked against the unchanged kernel forcebalance class. p4 now has checked smooth instances at realistic field strength and β.

title: Symmetry plus Noether confines every slow enough orbit forever.
text: symmetry plus noether confines every slow enough orbit forever. canonical momentum m⟨k,v⟩ + qψ is conserved for any killing symmetry k; with speed conservation and an intermediate-value argument, orbits stay in a flux region for all time. p3 has checked full-orbit instances; field lines are confined by exact first integrals.

title: The remaining device work is explicit.
text: the remaining device work is explicit. the vacuum-fixture work packages remain, now joined by an equilibrium/stability track. a four-circular-coil, cnt-inspired architecture is a reference direction, not a certified design. reusable mathematics now spans fields, equilibria, local stability and symmetric confinement. no practical build or energization specification has been released.

title: A burning plasma that provably stays above 10 keV.
text: a burning plasma that provably stays above 10 kev. a reactor-scale 0-d d-t plasma (n = 10²⁰ m⁻³, 830 m³, carbon impurities with z_eff = 1.7) stays at or above 10 kev for all t ≥ 0 once heating beats losses at 10 kev. radial transport obeys a proved comparison principle, so a barrier profile bounds the temperature everywhere for all time. 13 new modules, including kernel laws for fusion power, radial transport and vacuum fields, each with sanity checks. an adversarial review caught a fuel-dilution error in the first m1 version; the kernel and the margins were corrected.

title: Every solution starting above the barrier keeps a 10 keV core forever.
text: every solution starting above the barrier keeps a 10 kev core forever. for the flux-surface heat equation with alpha heating, bremsstrahlung and ≈70 mw of deposited heating, a certified barrier profile bounds the temperature from below for all time. a 0-d burn window now follows from the ipb98(y,2) confinement scaling instead of ad-hoc confinement-time assumptions. 14 new modules. reviews found no soundness bugs and led to guards for shearless mercier surfaces, a non-vacuity witness for the obstruction, and clarified χ normalization and corner compatibility.

title: Every 3.5 MeV alpha born in the core stays in — forever.
text: every 3.5 mev alpha born in the core stays in — forever. in an exact equilibrium satisfying j × b = ∇p at 5 t and β ≈ 4.6%, every fusion alpha with energy ≤ 3.5 mev starting in the inner quarter of the flux, with any pitch, stays inside the plasma for all time under the full lorentz force. the margin is 1.5%: the same argument fails at 3.7 mev. 15 new modules and a recorded kernel change. three review passes: pressure consistency of the barrier, a finite-time boozer orbit structure, a kernel law excluding vacuous regular axes, and non-vacuity witnesses.

title: From 0.8 ms to 0.11 s — and a plasma equilibrium validated to 10⁻¹¹.
text: from 0.8 ms to 0.11 s — and a plasma equilibrium validated to 10⁻¹¹. iterating an oscillatory averaging lemma three times, with exact lie-derivative amplitudes and certified enclosures, extends passing-alpha confinement in a reactor-scale near-axis quasisymmetric field from 0.8 ms to 0.11 s. a slab grad–shafranov equilibrium with an exponential pressure profile is validated by the radii polynomial and proved to satisfy the kernel force balance. 12 new modules. reviews found an oracle factor-of-2 error (corrected; conclusion unchanged) and no soundness defects in the averaged-trapping theorem; its ≈ 6 min build is scheduled for a proof-term rewrite.

title: Confinement and heat, proved for the same field, with a pressure budget.
text: confinement and heat, proved for the same field, with a pressure budget. solovev_one_plasma: one exact solov'ev field satisfying j × b = ∇p with pressure p_eq + 40 kpa; every 3.5 mev alpha born in the core stays inside forever (full lorentz orbits); every classical solution of the transport model starting in a certified band (existence assumed, not proved) keeps a ≥ 10 kev core forever, with plasma pressure within the budget ≤ p_eq + 40 kpa — bounded by it, not equal to the force-balance pressure. 8 new modules and kernel change k2. a sub-agent report that claimed non-existent geometry lemmas was caught at integration; every cited declaration is now grep-checked.

title: No supplied geometry, no auxiliary power — and a genuine stellarator field.
text: no supplied geometry, no auxiliary power — and a genuine stellarator field. the pressure-budget theorem (transport solutions supplied) now uses flux-surface quantities computed from the equilibrium itself. with quarter-kev reactivity data it certifies a high-q (q ≈ 40) band and an ignited band with zero auxiliary heating. separately, an exact rational vacuum field with two field periods and stellarator symmetry gives the library its first non-axisymmetric stellarator geometry. 13 new modules; review found no bugs (fine windows and geometry bounds independently recomputed). trapped near-qa alphas: turning points proved, non-resonance open — a real resonance exists in the band.

title: 95 toroidal transits, certified, in a genuine stellarator field.
text: 95 toroidal transits, certified, in a genuine stellarator field. for the exact vacuum field b = ∇φ + ¼∇h — non-axisymmetric, two field periods, stellarator-symmetric — every field line starting within ≈ 0.023 r₀ of the magnetic axis stays within ≈ 0.1 r₀ of it for at least 95 full toroidal transits. and the coarea formula closes the last stated geometric link in the pressure-budget theorem (transport solutions are still supplied). 7 new modules; review found the certificate sound (exact margins, symmetry reduction and face coverage checked) and led to a local field-line version and fuller disclosures.

title: Stable on every surface; from coil error to confined field lines.
text: stable on every surface; from coil error to confined field lines. ideal ballooning is certified on every flux surface of the reactor equilibrium, axis to edge. for the exact stellarator field, a concrete closed filament reproduces the toroidal part to 2.5×10⁻⁶, and any coil set whose helical error on a bounding surface is below 6.5×10⁻⁴ (or 5.6×10⁻⁵) inherits 1 (or 10) certified transits. 33 new modules (many certificate cells). the ballooning certificate was rebuilt as a proof-term cover; the trapped-alpha cell checks still await that rewrite.

title: Finite pressure without axisymmetry — and all-time confinement from one torus.
text: finite pressure without axisymmetry — and all-time confinement from one torus. landreman's family-1 equilibrium satisfies the kernel force balance with finite pressure, is genuinely non-axisymmetric with a non-planar axis, and has all field lines closed and confined. for the exact stellarator vacuum field, any invariant torus traps every field line inside it forever. 3 new modules and two theory notes; a discovery-note error about the family-1 axis was caught and corrected by the formalization.

title: A certified approximate torus and the first KAM lemmas.
text: a certified approximate torus and the first kam lemmas. torus a — a 2-d fourier embedding with rational coefficients — solves the field-line invariance equation of the exact stellarator field to 10⁻²³ for all angles, and is a radial graph around the magnetic axis. the diophantine and cohomological lemmas of kam theory are proved with explicit constants. 7 new modules. constants budget for the kam step is an informal estimate until the frame and twist certificates land.

title: Real coils, certified field lines.
text: real coils, certified field lines. eight closed polygonal helical filaments plus a closed toroidal-field filament produce a field whose lines, starting near the axis, stay in the confinement tube for a full toroidal transit — proved from the exact biot–savart field of straight segments, a certified 6.5×10⁻⁴ frontier error and the vacuum maximum principle. 25 new modules; review found the coil chain sound (segment formula, corners, cover, symmetry, avoidance) and led to zero-margin and existence disclosures.

title: Error, frame, twist and small divisors — all certified.
text: error, frame, twist and small divisors — all certified. for torus a of the exact stellarator field: weighted invariance error ≤ 6×10⁻²² on a complex strip, a symplectic frame with explicit inverse bounds, twist ≥ 3/10, and diophantine constant 0.0687. a sheared finite-β non-axisymmetric equilibrium joins the library. 10 new modules completing the kam input certificates and adding family 2.

title: An exact invariant torus, and field lines trapped for all time.
text: an exact invariant torus, and field lines trapped for all time. a verified kam theorem turns the certified approximate torus (error 10⁻²²) into an exact real-analytic invariant torus of the stellarator field with rotational transform (75 + √5)/562. by the torus-trapping theorem, every field line starting inside it — at least 0.077 r₀ from the axis — stays inside forever. 17 new modules completing the kam route; the frame-transport assumption from part 3 is now derived.

title: An exact torus for alpha guiding centres; coils need new analysis.
text: an exact torus for alpha guiding centres; coils need new analysis. passing (μ = 0) guiding centres follow field lines of b + ρ_s∇×b. for 3.5 mev alphas at b₀r₀ ≈ 69 t·m (ρ_s = 1/256) this field has an exact invariant torus, proved with a kam theorem extended to an inverse-square-root node. the analogous result for the coil-produced field is blocked by a 39-order-of-magnitude gap. about 75 new modules (many certificates); the vacuous coil certificate is committed but excluded from the default build.

title: Passing 3.5 MeV alpha guiding centres never leave the torus.
text: passing 3.5 mev alpha guiding centres never leave the torus. with the exact torus of the guiding-centre field b + (1/256)∇×b and b*∥ = |b|, every μ = 0 littlejohn orbit of a 3.5 mev alpha with v∥ > 0 that starts inside the torus — in the stellarator field scaled to b₀r₀ ≈ 69 t·m — stays inside for all time, and such orbits exist from every interior point. 7 new modules finishing the guiding-centre route (generic flowtorus layer, star-shapedness certificates, orbit-to-field-line reduction).

title: A family of exact tori over a range of B₀R₀.
text: a family of exact tori over a range of b₀r₀. a chebyshev-in-ρ family of approximate tori, certified uniformly by kronecker-ball arithmetic, gives an exact invariant torus of the guiding-centre field for every ρ_s in an interval — hence all-time confinement of passing alpha guiding centres for every b₀r₀ ∈ [67.95, 69.99] t·m. a second torus covers v∥ < 0. about 90 new modules (mostly certificates).

title: Finite pressure, no axisymmetry — and Mercier-stable.
text: finite pressure, no axisymmetry — and mercier-stable. landreman family 2 at λ = 200 is mercier-stable on every flux surface k ∈ [0.7, 0.9], certified by validated quadrature with a fully proved checker. the surfaces have a magnetic hill; shear stabilizes them at low β. about 40 new modules; review found the checker sound and the label gap, now disclosed.

title: A cone of pitch angles, confined forever.
text: a cone of pitch angles, confined forever. passing guiding centres with μ > 0 follow field lines of b + ∇×(ρ_{e,μ}b). a chebyshev family of exact tori in λ = μb₀/e ∈ [0, 1/16] traps every passing 3.5 mev alpha guiding centre starting inside — and proves it stays passing. about 120 new modules (mostly certificates).

title: Positive measure in velocity space — in a narrow energy band.
text: positive measure in velocity space — in a narrow energy band. tori certified at four energies are interpolated with a proved analytic remainder. every passing alpha guiding centre with |e − 3.5 mev| ≤ 0.4 ev and λ ∈ [0, 1/16] starting inside an exact torus stays inside, and stays passing, forever. a second pitch cell extends the one-energy result to λ ∈ [0, 1/8]. about 440 new files, nearly all certificate modules outside the default build.

title: Reduced exactly to one inequality — but not yet certified.
text: reduced exactly to one inequality — but not yet certified. a general 3-d surface ballooning framework reduces stability of every field line and every θ_k on a family-2 surface to one pointwise inequality on surface × ℝ. the secular part of that inequality is now solved exactly in lean. numerically the band is stable, but no certificate has been found. five modules join the default build.

title: Search on a big machine; re-check on the laptop.
text: search on a big machine; re-check on the laptop. heavy numerics and first builds of large certificates run on a workstation and are pushed to workstation/* branches; the laptop re-checks them within its build budget before merging. no theorem comes from the workstation yet; merged lean must still build on the laptop.

title: Every pitch parameter up to λ = 1/4 — at one energy.
text: every pitch parameter up to λ = 1/4 — at one energy. five certified pitch cells, three of them computed on the workstation, combine into one theorem: passing 3.5 mev alpha guiding centres with any μ ∈ [0, e/(4b₀)] starting inside an exact torus stay inside, and stay passing, forever. λ = 1/4 is the limit of the present passing argument. the pitch range now reaches the limit of the passing argument with |b| ≤ 3b₀.

title: Fewer decide +kernel: checks become explicit, inductive certificates.
text: fewer decide +kernel: checks become explicit, inductive certificates. large numerical checks are rebuilt in the subsetsum pattern: an inductive certificate predicate with one constructor per local step, soundness by induction, a meta builder, and small kernel nat leaves. kernel-check memory was halved first. theorem statements are unchanged; bridges re-prove the original checks.

title: Eleven workstation runs, with failures recorded as carefully as successes.
text: eleven workstation runs, with failures recorded as carefully as successes. the workstation computed two pitch cells and migrated the on-demand families to proof terms; the laptop reviewed every run and merged the ones that passed. all runs are listed in workstation/reviewed.md.

title: First strict audit: kernel, models and claims checked; overclaims corrected.
text: first strict audit: kernel, models and claims checked; overclaims corrected. audited commit cda8bd0 (30 october 2026): every kernel declaration, the twelve model definitions behind the headline results, repository scans and a trace of every headline claim to its lean statement. no critical findings and no false proof. the foundation is now audited under the strict protocol; findings and fixes are recorded in the plan and in notes/audit/.

title: A Grad counterexample, a quasisymmetry barrier, and a current finding — infrastructure under the contract.
text: a grad counterexample, a quasisymmetry barrier, and a current finding — infrastructure under the contract. new theory since the strict audit. under the contract these are mathematical infrastructure or barriers, not design progress: they establish non-symmetry or rule out a route, while c1 and c2 need current-free, omnigenous candidates. all in the default build with standard axioms only. next under the contract: a dommaschk qa vacuum fit (c1 by construction), drift and ε_eff diagnostics on the rational field, and lean definitions for c1 and c2.

title: Working with the agents: start, work status, work on, keep working.
text: working with the agents: start, work status, work on, keep working. theory is built as well as formalized while designing stellarators. work is a research graph of goals (g-*), questions (q-*) and notes (n-*); lean is the validity gate, so a result is established only when its named declaration compiles. the plasmalean-develop-theory skill and the research-graph registries are in place; after every stage of progress the agents update notes and slides, regenerate the site, commit and push.

title: Plan of record: the stellarator contract and a research graph of goals, questions and notes.
text: plan of record: the stellarator contract and a research graph of goals, questions and notes. since 30 october the plan is organized by the contract c1–c5 and a research graph (goals g-*, questions q-*, notes n-*). current-free and omnigenous candidates come first, ahead of further non-axisymmetry results; lean remains the validity gate. phases 1–16 and the model ladder m0–m5 are kept as history in the plan; the research graph maps their results to goals g-1–g-11 and records the strict-audit findings.

title: The next run must leave evidence, not just a promise.
text: the next run must leave evidence, not just a promise. next, in the contract's priority order: a dommaschk qa vacuum fit with certified tori and ι ≥ ι_min; drift and ε_eff diagnostics on the exact rational field; the net current of the landreman families; lean definitions for c1 and c2 with the sanity triad; then a current-free finite-β equilibrium and thermal neoclassical bounds for c5. the linked run records checked declarations, assumptions and validation. this slideshow is a summary of that evidence, not a new design certificate.
